## CC-124 · Standing article production (decision 39)
- Outcome: each run publishes one new, useful article, then stops. The lane runner starts this item ahead of the queue once 2 hours have passed since its last start (`Cadence: 120 min` on the Owner line; CC-256 R3), and again whenever no other Publisher item is OPEN, until the day's target of 8 distinct articles is met (the production-day record).
  - Pick the best due piece, in this order:
    1. event previews and reviews that are due (CC-107; the midterm preview from `A:\Capital Chronicle\ResearchRuns\claude-main-events-20261029\20261103-midterm-dossier\PREVIEW.md` once it exists; NFP on 6 Nov);
    2. today's official releases and market moves;
    3. Tier 1 company pieces from the CC-036 and CC-040 digests;
    4. CFTC positioning (CC-018);
    5. CC-074 retrospectives (the latest CPI, NFP and PPI before 28 Oct, and the ECB's October decision).
  - Write, edit and review with the approved roles, with charts where the data supports them and text otherwise. Publish to Substack and the text channels, read back, and record the result in this item's Result line, for example "+1: <title>, <Substack URL>".
  - Start no operation while a newsroom window holds its lease, and never run two at once. If nothing passes the guards, end the run with the first blocking cause.
- Acceptance: published articles with readback, counted daily in the production-day record and the 07:00 digest (CC-122).
- Ops, 3 Nov 03:00 GMT+7: a standing item keeps Status OPEN after every run. Put the run's result in the Result line. When nothing is due yet, write `Status: OPEN (next due <d MMM yyyy HH:mm> GMT+7)`. The runner restarts it after that time and at least 45 minutes after its last start. Only Ops writes PAUSED.
- Ops, 3 Nov 03:01 GMT+7: while the next publication is not yet due (the 3-hour gap), a run still writes, edits and reviews the next article, so it is ready to send. It publishes only at or after the due time, and the next run sends it then. Never end a run idle when an article can be prepared.
- Ops, 3 Nov 08:03 GMT+7: Substack publication is blocked: at 23:08Z the September CPI retrospective (draft 223246940) stopped at SUBSTACK_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED and is a draft with UNKNOWN_WRITE. Jim completes Substack's email verification for that draft. Publisher then reads it back and continues; it never makes a replacement draft or repeats the send. The midterm preview (CC-107) comes first once Substack works.
- Ops, 3 Nov 11:31 GMT+7, Jim's decision 44: private surveys (ISM, S&P Global PMI, Conference Board, UMich, ADP) appear only as an attributed headline figure, never as tables, charts or history. A single consensus figure may be quoted with attribution. Charts use public-domain official series and the desk's own work.
- Ops, 3 Nov 13:04 GMT+7: Substack is drafts only. Codex Publisher saves each finished article, with its charts and visuals, as a Substack draft and never presses Publish or Update there, so no Substack code is triggered by the pipeline. Jim publishes the drafts himself. The site and social posts go out without Substack (decision 48). Never read a mailbox or enter a code.
- Ops, 3 Nov 15:27 GMT+7, Jim's decision 52: this replaces the 13:04 drafts-only rule. At the end of every article Publisher presses every publish button, Substack (web-only, decision 42) included. When Substack asks for the email code, Publisher leaves that BrowserOS Neo tab open on the code screen, records PENDING_JIM_EMAIL_CODE and carries on in other tabs; Jim enters the code. Never read a mailbox or enter a code.
- Ops, 3 Nov 17:57 GMT+7: Substack publish routine (Jim's decision 54): before pressing Publish, keep two tabs in the same BrowserOS Neo window: Jim's Gmail inbox tab, open and untouched (agents never read it), and the Substack draft. When the "Check your email" dialog appears, record PENDING_JIM_EMAIL_CODE and wait on that tab: no reload, no other field typed, no other tab used. Jim types the 6-digit code. When the URL moves to /publish/posts/detail/.../share-center, continue with readback and the dispatch record. This replaces the decision 52 instruction to carry on in other tabs.
- Ops, 4 Nov 19:40 GMT+7: Jim, 19:40 GMT+7, found today's posts broken on every destination: the SEC roundtable post has a wrong image on Substack, Telegram, Facebook, Discord, X, YouTube and Instagram; two Substack posts are faulty; LinkedIn and Threads have nothing since last week; Instagram has 3 posts and YouTube 4. He moved the root-cause fix and completion of ContentOps V1 to a new Claude lane; Codex keeps writing and posting afterwards. Ops stopped the Codex Publisher runner at 19:40 so the two do not collide; it restarts after the lane's report.
- Ops Product, 5 Nov 05:12 GMT+7 (CC-256 R3): on 4 Nov no article run started for 15.4 h (06:25-21:51Z) while 20 runs of 13 other items went first. `lane_runner.ps1` (hash 9F73285F…, backup `lane_runner.ps1.backup-20261105-pre-r3`) now starts the standing item first when its Owner line names a `Cadence: <n> min` and its last run folder is at least that old; PAUSED, "next due", the 45-minute gap and the daily cap still apply. Dry-run on a copy: no folder → due; 30 min → not due; 150 min → due; Data (no token) unchanged. The runners load it between runs by themselves. Done when: a day with OPEN Publisher items shows an article run at least every 2 hours in runner-publisher.log.
- Ops Product, 5 Nov 10:20 GMT+7: two pipeline tests fail on the live head since your 6b83091e and 49b238d0: `tests/test_eight_platform_substack_first_pipeline_v1.py::test_instagram_consumes_only_verified_delivery_manifest_media` and `::test_instagram_fails_definite_no_write_without_verified_delivery_media` (found by the ContentOps V1 lane on 5e18ce51).
  - 49b238d0 adds `require_publication_image` before Discord, Facebook, Instagram and Threads writes (`_eight_platform_substack_first_pipeline_impl_v1.py:4281`).
  - Before the next Instagram write, settle which it is: the fixtures lack the new image binding (update them), or the guard refuses a valid post (fix it). Then report which.
- Ops Product, 5 Nov 14:13 GMT+7: in your post-writer card step, pass the written article to the card builder; never build cards against a stand-in article made of the card's own sentences (as `run-20261105-0832/build_media.py` did). On IBM that stand-in card was excluded by the publication view (DATA_CARD_FACT_OR_NUMBER_NOT_IN_POST_AND_SOURCE), and Substack waited 18 minutes. Since ContentOps 33beb6cb (CC-290), the card builder finds the article's own sentences itself, so the stand-in is no longer needed.
- Ops Product, 5 Nov 15:03 GMT+7 (Jim's decision 79, plus his 15:01 GMT+7 note that Codex has quota again): focus on decision 79's content.
  - Daily pieces for gold, US500, EURUSD, USDJPY, USOIL and BTCUSD, read against US10Y.
  - The event pieces: NFP on Fri 6 Nov, CPI on Tue 10 Nov.
  - Once CC-306 is live, one short post per change of plan state.
  Plain wording per section 4.4: no ids or internal words, decision 40's notice, and no filler. The cadence stays at 120 min, which is enough for these.
- Ops Product, 6 Nov 01:53 GMT+7 (Jim's decision 89): from now on, articles come only from Main's reports: the six markets' plans and views, event dossiers (NFP, CPI), decision records and the scorecard. No news briefs from headlines. When Main has nothing new, the run ends at once with no filler.
- Ops Product, 6 Nov 21:03 GMT+7 (Jim's decision 93), from the next run:
  - never reuse an image: no Federal Reserve building photograph again, and every piece gets a lead image not published before;
  - at most two articles a day, with a run every 6 hours;
  - every piece has a scenarios section (2-3 scenarios, each with its labelled model-estimate probability, confirmation, market moves and invalidation), and every social copy carries the base case and the main alternative.
  CC-333 builds the guard.
- Ops Product, 6 Nov 22:05 GMT+7 (Jim's weekend load rule, 6 Nov about 15:00Z): on Sat 7 and Sun 8 Nov, at most one article a day, only from a new Main report, with a run every 12 hours. The normal cadence (every 6 hours, at most 2 a day) returns Mon 9 Nov 01:00 GMT+7. Codex Publisher takes no new build until then, except CC-333.
- Owner: Codex Publisher · Risk: content · Due: standing · Effort: max · Cadence: 360 min, at most 2 articles a day · Status: IN_PROGRESS (Codex Publisher, 8 Nov 2026 17:25 GMT+7)
- Branch: backlog/cc-124-main-source-check-20261108-1725 · Result: +0: JIM_DECISION_93_MAIN_SCENARIOS_INCOMPLETE (40/40 alternatives lack probability); chose preserve NFP request because Main has no complete scenario set; 20438e9e pushed/live; 10 checks PASS, docs/publisher/CC-124/run-20261108-0352/README.md; Main supplies dated probabilities and six-market implications; Sol 6.1/max CONFIGURED_NOT_OBSERVED.
